article_title: Stress, stressors and related factors in clinical learning of midwifery students in Iran: a cross sectional study.
citation: Rezaei Behrooz, Falahati Juliana, Beheshtizadeh Raziyeh. (2020). Stress, stressors and related factors in clinical learning of midwifery students in Iran: a cross sectional study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-1970-7
title: Persian Questionnaire of Stressful Sources (PQSS) for clinical learning stressors
description: The PQSS is a 29-item, four-point Likert questionnaire developed by Iranian researchers that "evaluates the sources of stress in clinical learning environment from nursing and midwifery students’ view point". It measures four dimensions: interpersonal communication (8 items), clinical practices (8 items), unpleasant emotions (7 items) and humiliating experiences (6 items), with total scores ranging from 29 to 116. In this study its reliability was confirmed with a Cronbach's alpha of 0.94, and it was administered alongside the Persian 14-item Cohen Perceived Stress Scale.
requirements: Respondents must have clinical learning experience; the study included only students who had passed at least one semester of internship
constraints: Test-retest reliability and content validity confirmed only in national (Iranian) studies; scores depend on self-report
target_learning_goals: identifying sources of stress in clinical learning environments
examples: Used in the 2016 cross-sectional survey of 70 Iranian midwifery students, yielding a total mean score of 2.14 ± 0.50 on a 1–4 scale
